## Intent
Exercise "transpose": implement `transpose`. Given an input text output it transposed. Roughly explained, the transpose of a matrix: ```text ABC DEF ``` is given by: ```text AD BE CF ``` Rows become columns and columns become rows. See [transpose][]. If the input has rows of different lengths, this is to be solved as follows: - Pad to the left with spaces. - Don't pad to the right. Therefore, transposing this matrix: ```text ABC DE ``` results in: ```text AD BE C ``` And transposing: ```text AB DEF ``` results in: ```text AD BE F ``` In general, all characters from the input should also be present in the transposed output. That means that if a column in the input text contains only spaces on its bottom-most row(s), the corresponding output row should contain the spaces in its right-most column(s). [transpose]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transpose Gold context (from the instructions and stub only):
- transpose(rows: string[]): string[]: input rows of text, output rows of the transposed text. Output row c is input column c read top to bottom; the number of output rows is the length of the longest input row.
- Rows of different lengths: pad to the LEFT with spaces, never pad to the right. A missing character in a column is a space only when some LATER row (below it) still has a character in that column; otherwise the output row just ends.
- All characters of the input appear in the output, including spaces: if an input column has only spaces in its bottom-most row(s), those spaces stay at the right end of the output row.
- Instruction examples: ["ABC","DEF"] -> ["AD","BE","CF"]; ["ABC","DE"] -> ["AD","BE","C"]; ["AB","DEF"] -> ["AD","BE"," F"].
- Useful built-ins: String.prototype.padEnd / padStart, String.prototype.charAt(i) (returns "" past the end), Math.max.
